_about: Curated judgements for the status report (owner: status-reporter). Read by scripts/status_report.py together with docs/features.json and the live board, gates and ledger. Everything here is a judgement that must be traceable to evidence ids listed under 'evidence'; the script refuses to render if the judgements contradict the gate checklists. Written for a technically capable reader who does not know the repo: spell out abbreviations, no file names or task ids in the executive fields.

project.name: HX Stomp Tone Matcher
project.goal: Give the tool a song and get back a preset for the Line 6 HX Stomp guitar pedal that sounds like the guitar on the recording, checked on the real pedal. It works by trying candidate presets, comparing the sound with the recording, and adjusting until they match.

health.rationale: Gate 2 attempt 3, run once on the fresh sealed set of 96 known-answer items, met all seven checks of the frozen rule: category 0.885 (bar 0.85), model 0.771 (bar 0.60), settings error 0.101 (bar 0.15), ranking the true preset first 0.979 (bar 0.95), better than the random walk on model (+0.208, interval low end +0.094) and on settings (-0.083, whole interval below zero), and the consistency split, which carries no information on this set. The ranking check was amended by the human before the run so that two settings differing only in volume count as a tie; attempts 1 and 2 keep their figures under the old rule. The gate is not passed until the human signs. At Risk rather than On Track: pedal results still cannot be counted, real songs are unmeasured, the test is the known-clean-recording case only, and delay model accuracy is weak (5 of 12).

technical.rationale: Engineering advanced a long way on 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-18: specialists for each effect family, a crash-safe parallel job runner that scales to the machine's core count, a portable load measure, a level-aware tie rule for the ranking check, a gain-aware score term, and a mod-family prior. Attempt 3 moved category to 0.885 and model to 0.771 and met every check. Advancing is earned on the known-answer test only; real songs and the pedal are not yet advanced.

breakdown.implemented: Control of both sound engines, preset reading and writing, guitar separation, a clean-guitar picker, tone-comparison measures (one admitted for the known-clean-recording case), an optimiser, a hybrid model-and-settings search, measured seeding, the 605-template Native library, the 96-item known-answer set and runner with the frozen pass rule, a block-presence detector, a chain-pattern prior, a chain builder (fake engines only), a cabinet-response estimator, a blind A/B tool, and verification suites for both engines. Since attempt 1: specialists for cabinet and equaliser, time-based effects, modulation, amp and gain, a family dispatcher, an elastic job runner, and a sealed fresh set (synthetic-v2).
breakdown.integrated: A hand-run script takes one prepared song section through separation, clean-guitar choice, search and preset export on one machine. The known-answer runner drives the hybrid search on the real Native engine. Nothing runs from a single command from a song to a pedal-checked preset; the chain builder has not been run on a real engine.
breakdown.tested: Last verified suite run: commit 68f0310, lint clean, 750 passed, 28 skipped on the committed set; no suite was run for this report (the lead runs it separately). Real Helix sound from Native was used for the tone-comparison test, the Native verification and the full 96-item known-answer run.
breakdown.verified: Software engine (Native): settings land exactly apart from recorded misses and renders repeat (216 of 216). Pedal: control, restore and layout agreement were verified on hardware earlier, but the new sampling checks found defects, and no pedal result counts until the residual USB slip is handled. Gate 2 attempt 1 measured model choice, category, settings and ranking on synthetic known-answer items. Matching on real songs is verified only by one informal listen. Gate 2 attempt 2 passed 6 of 7 checks and attempt 3 passed all 7 on 96 sealed synthetic items each (ledger 2026-10-18T15:46:15 for attempt 3), awaiting the human's sign-off.
breakdown.unfinished: The human's Gate 2 sign-off, delay model accuracy (5 of 12) and drive (7 of 12), the pedal-side fixes, the chain builder on a real engine, a one-command song-to-preset tool, blind listening, real-song separation measurement, and anything beyond macOS.

readiness.rationale: Important pieces are demonstrated: a real song was matched by a script and listened to, the tone comparison passes on single blocks with a known clean recording, and the known-answer run now meets every Gate 2 check (category 88.5 percent, model 77 percent of 96 sealed items, settings close). Gate 2 is not signed yet, so the system cannot be called Validated, and the pieces are not shown to work together from a song to a pedal-checked preset.
readiness.blocker_to_next: Integrated needs one command from song to a pedal-checked preset, a chain builder that has run on a real engine, and a comparison that works without a lined-up clean recording. Validated also needs the human's Gate 2 sign-off.

summary: The goal is a tool that listens to a recorded guitar tone and builds a matching preset for the HX Stomp pedal. The third attempt at Gate 2, the known-answer test on 96 single effects, met all seven agreed checks: the tool names the effect category 88.5 percent of the time and the exact model 77 percent, finds close settings, beats a random-guess baseline, and its comparison score ranks the true preset first on 94 of 96 items. The gate is not passed until the owner signs it. The ranking check was relaxed by the owner beforehand so that settings differing only in loudness count as a tie, and this is the known-clean-recording case only. The weakest effect is now delay (5 of 12 exact models, mostly one delay mistaken for another). Nothing yet turns a song into a finished preset in one step.

biggest_problem.why: With Gate 2 awaiting the owner's sign-off, the weakest measured part of the method is delay: the exact model was named on only 5 of 12 delay items on the sealed set (drive 7, amp 8; cabinet 12). Four of the seven misses name a different delay model, which may still sound close, and three name a different kind of effect. It is not a gate issue, but delay is common in real tones, so it is the next target for the search and the next thing to listen to (the Gate 2 page has the delay misses with the target on the left channel and our guess on the right).

Gate 1.goal: Prove both sound engines can be driven by code, and that a generated preset loads on the pedal.
criteria_plain: Helix Native renders a test clip from code (smoke test passes).
The HX Stomp renders the same test clip from code on at least one operating system.
A generated preset file is accepted by HX Edit and loads on the pedal.
The shared engine interface is frozen and the control routes are documented.
Gate 1.demonstrated: All four criteria are evidenced and the owner signed off on 2026-10-14. Caveats the owner accepted: the pedal result rested on one operating system and firmware 3.50 (the pedal has since been updated to 3.80 and its smoke test passes there); the pedal-load result was reported by the owner, not observed by an automated test.
Gate 1.remaining: Nothing for the gate itself. Windows and Linux pedal control remain unverified.
Gate 1.next_action: None. The pedal is now on firmware 3.80 and its smoke test passes there; the remaining 3.80 re-checks (parity with Native) belong to the next gate.

Gate 2.goal: Show the tool can recover a known answer: given audio made from a preset we already know, its comparison measure picks the true preset and its search finds the right blocks and settings, at thresholds agreed in advance.
criteria_plain: On the known-answer set, the tone-comparison measure ranks the true preset first at the agreed threshold.
Block types, amp and effect models, and parameter values are identified within the agreed accuracy.
A curve showing how accuracy falls as guitar separation gets worse has been recorded.
Gate 2.demonstrated: Attempt 3 ran on all 96 sealed synthetic-v3 items (ledger 2026-10-18T15:46:15): all 7 checks met. Category 0.885 (bar 0.85), model 0.771 (bar 0.60), settings error 0.101 (bar 0.15), ranking the true preset first 0.979, 94 of 96 (bar 0.95; misses i039 and i095, both cabinets), model against the random walk +0.208 (interval low end +0.094, needs -0.05), settings against the random walk -0.083 (whole interval below zero). The consistency split carries no information on this set. The ranking check used the owner's extended rule B (volume-only matches count as ties), amended before the run; attempts 1 and 2 keep their old-rule figures (attempt 1 met 5 of 7, attempt 2 met 6 of 7, rank-1 0.9375). The separation stress curve is ticked from 2026-10-16. Only the owner's sign-off is missing.
Gate 2.remaining: The owner's sign-off. Later work (not a gate condition): delay model accuracy, drive, and real songs.
Gate 2.blocking: Awaiting the owner's sign-off (2026-10-18). No check is failing.
Gate 2.next_action: Owner: sign Gate 2 or say what is missing. The gate ledger row is written only with the sign-off.

Gate 3.goal: Show that the tool can match clean recordings of real guitar pedals, judged by re-rendering the matched preset from a held-out dry take and by a short blind listen.
criteria_plain: A dry reference of the player's guitar (random playing) has been captured; it is the only dry signal the matcher may use.
A set of single real pedals (one per available category, several random settings each) has been recorded, with the matching dry take kept aside for scoring.
The matched presets meet a quality bar set before the run, and a short blind listen agrees.
Two- and three-pedal chains have been recorded and matched by the chain builder at the same bar.
Gate 3.demonstrated: Nothing yet: no dry reference, pedal recording or real-pedal match exists. Some groundwork carries over (the chain builder tested with fake engines, the blind listening tool), but none of it has been run on real pedals.
Gate 3.remaining: Capture the dry reference and the single-pedal set, choose the quality bar before the run, then record and match two- and three-pedal chains. The matcher must work without a lined-up dry take (note-invariant comparison terms, a learned guitar embedding, a phase-insensitive modulation score).
Gate 3.blocking: Depends on Gate 2 and on the player recording the pedals.
Gate 3.next_action: Wait for Gate 2; the player can plan the recording session.

Gate 4.goal: Show that, for real songs, the tool's preset beats the nearest ready-made community preset in blind listening.
criteria_plain: In blind listening on a 20-song set, the matched preset is preferred over the nearest community preset on most songs.
The difference between the pedal and Native on firmware 3.80 has been recorded.
Native-mode and pedal-mode matching have been compared on the same songs.
Gate 4.demonstrated: One song section was matched and listened to informally (not blind). Pedal-versus-Native agreement on firmware 3.80 is recorded (ticked). Groundwork: a chain-pattern prior from 2,068 curated presets with strong order rules, a block-presence detector (only the cabinet and gain-stage calls pass, so it is a soft hint), a chain builder tested with fake engines, a cabinet-response study, and a blind A/B listening tool (built; no session rated). The Native-versus-pedal comparison on songs has not been run.
Gate 4.remaining: Gate 2, the chain builder on a real engine, the pedal verification fixes, the 20-song set, blind sessions, and the Native-versus-pedal comparison on songs. A full-library test is not planned (human decision).
Gate 4.blocking: Depends on Gate 2, on the chain builder, on the pedal fixes, and on song selection.
Gate 4.next_action: Wait for Gate 2. The owner can start choosing songs now.

issues.title: Delay is the weakest effect: 5 of 12 exact models on the sealed set
issues.problem: On Gate 2 attempt 3 (96 sealed items, all seven checks met) the exact model was right on cab 12, eq 11, reverb 11, mod 10, comp 10, amp 8, drive 7 and delay 5 of 12. The seven delay misses: four named another delay model (i001, i049, i073, i089), three a different kind of effect (i041 a compressor, i065 and i081 an equaliser). Two ranking misses (i039, i095) are cabinets.
issues.impact: Does not block Gate 2, which met every check, but delay is common in real tones and the model is wrong on more than half of the delay items. Real songs will be harder than this known-clean-recording test.
issues.cause: Not yet diagnosed. Swell-type and ducked delays look similar to other delays at the settings drawn; v3 is now seen, so diagnosis must use the development sets.
issues.resolution: Diagnose the delay misses on development data (echo time, feedback and mix versus model), then strengthen the time-based specialist; listen to the delay misses to see whether the swaps matter by ear.
issues.owner: search builds the delay work; the human listens; the lead schedules
issues.next_step: Listen to the delay misses on the Gate 2 page, then decide the order of work.

issues.title: No pedal measurement counts until the sampling defects are handled
issues.problem: The pedal verification found real defects: the audio stream over USB is not stable for about 0.7 s after it starts, amps carry sound over from the previous render, the pedal refuses four effect models in whole-preset writes, and some delay and reverb settings glide slowly when changed in place. Setting truth passed 20 of 40 items, repeatability 12 of 17. A longer pre-roll fixed the first problem, but a one-sample slip still happens about once in 90 renders. The human confirmed the pedal's blocks are editable after sessions.
issues.impact: The pedal is the final judge of the preset. Until the slip is detected or re-taken, pedal numbers cannot be used as evidence, and earlier pedal agreement figures are understated in noise. Gate 2 (Native only) is not affected; Gate 4 is.
issues.cause: Known for each defect (stream start-up, amp state, device refusals, parameter glide). The remaining slip has no recorded cause.
issues.resolution: Detect and re-take slipped renders, find why four models are refused, measure or avoid the parameter glide, then re-register the pedal rules (float32 read-back, an absolute -60 dB settle criterion, floors from rested renders) and re-run.
issues.owner: stomp-engine; the lead schedules the re-run
issues.next_step: Detect or re-take slipped renders, then fix the refusals and the glide.

issues.title: The tone comparison is only admitted when the clean recording is known
issues.problem: The tool's comparison measure passed its registered test on single-block Helix sound (0.990 against a bar of 0.90), but only for the case where the clean guitar recording behind the target is known and lined up. The earlier tests of the song case, where no clean recording exists, failed (about 7 correct in 40 on different notes). The song case with a separation stand-in reached 0.948 on single blocks and is not yet admitted; drive effects are its weak category.
issues.impact: Gate 2 can be passed on this footing, but real songs have no lined-up clean recording, so Gate 4 matching has no validated score yet. On the one real song tried, the top two candidates were nearly tied.
issues.cause: Level-free spectral comparison works when the notes match; it reacts to which notes were played when they do not. Four of seven test misses were drive Output changes, which this measure cannot see by design (a level guard handles loudness).
issues.resolution: Admit the song case separately once an aligned recording exists, add note-proof measures for the no-recording case (deferred option C), and re-test on real separated songs.
issues.next_step: Propose admission of the separated-song case with the drive weakness named; defer note-proof measures until Gate 4 planning.

issues.title: Guitar separation quality on real songs is unknown
issues.problem: Guitar separation has been scored only on artificial mixes: quality falls from 21.2 dB (guitar alone) to 7.3 dB with a second guitar in the mix. No real song has a quality score.
issues.impact: If the isolated guitar on a real song contains drums, vocals or artefacts, the tone comparison will chase those instead of the guitar and Gate 4 results will be unreliable.
issues.cause: No real-song stress set exists, and the only separation model aimed at guitar has no stated licence so it was not used.
issues.resolution: Run the separation stress test on a few real songs, locally, and record how accuracy falls as the mix gets denser.
issues.owner: separation, after the owner supplies songs
issues.next_step: Owner chooses the first songs (one action covers this and the Gate 4 song set).

issues.title: Building whole chains from single blocks is not yet shown to work
issues.problem: Single blocks are matched first and whole chains are built from analysis: the kinds of block present, ordered by common patterns. The pattern prior now rests on 2,068 curated presets and shows strong order rules. But the block-presence detector passed its test only for the cabinet and for whether a gain stage is present; for delay, reverb and modulation it missed its bars. The chain builder exists and is tested only with fake engines.
issues.impact: Gate 4 (real songs) needs whole chains. Presence is used only as a soft hint, so every time-based block must be confirmed by rendering with and without it.
issues.cause: Behind an amp and cabinet, single-block detectors call the extra block a drive almost every time; comparing against the clean recording cannot isolate a block that follows a non-linear amp.
issues.resolution: Judge post-amp blocks against the chain's current best render, render a multi-block test set on Native, and run the chain builder on a real engine. Cabinet choice by deconvolution looks promising.
issues.next_step: Schedule the multi-block render set; this is Gate 4 work and does not block Gate 2.

issues.title: The pedal and Native disagree on one cabinet setting
issues.problem: The cabinet's Early Reflections setting does not sound the same on the pedal and in Native.
issues.impact: A preset found on the fast Native engine can sound different on the real pedal. At the value the search chose, the two engines' recordings cancel by only 3.6 dB (poor agreement); with the setting at 0 they cancel by 31 dB (close agreement).
issues.cause: Not yet known. Candidates are an older algorithm in the pedal, a different parameter scale, or a delay-structure difference. Other parameters tested at their extremes agreed.
issues.resolution: Find the cause, or measure every searchable parameter on both engines and let the search free only the parameters that agree.
issues.owner: native-engine and stomp-engine; benchmark for the per-parameter audit
issues.next_step: Keep the setting at 0 for pedal presets and let the pedal check it (the accepted rule); the verification suites cover settings generally.

issues.title: Native verification leaves recorded misses that are explained, not fixed
issues.problem: After three engine fixes (baked controls no longer sent, hosts that start in the other numeric mode are re-prepared, a state latch from the first amp loaded), repeatability is 216 of 216 and nothing unexplained remains. Two rules still miss as written: setting truth 116 of 120 and baked values 63 of 73. Seven misses are one-step float rounding in how Native lands a control value; seven are effect-loop and send blocks.
issues.impact: None blocks Gate 2 (ruled acceptable on 2026-10-17). Native results produced before the fixes were made by the earlier engine and may differ by rounding up to about -21 dB on a few chains.
issues.cause: Native's own arithmetic and the nature of input and output blocks.
issues.resolution: Exclude those blocks from search pools (done), and re-state the rule with a one-step tolerance for the next version.
issues.owner: native-engine; the lead owns the rule wording
issues.next_step: None needed before the second Gate 2 attempt.

issues.title: The software engine cannot stand in for every pedal effect
issues.problem: Measurements show Native can stand in for the pedal on amps, cabinets, dynamics, equalisers, most drives, delays, Room, Plate, Spring and Chamber reverbs, Hall above 500 Hz, and the modulation effects. It cannot for Ganymede-type reverbs, Hall on bass-heavy material, Bitcrusher-type drives and the cabinet Early Reflections setting, and blocks that modulate on their own are left out of the search unless asked for.
issues.impact: Presets that use those effects must be checked on the pedal, which is slower; the block library also has no measured fingerprints yet, so models are not yet chosen from measurements.
issues.cause: The two engines run some effects differently, and Native's control steps limit fine settings (now 10 ms for delay time instead of 63 ms).
issues.resolution: Keep the pedal as the checker for the listed effects; finish the block fingerprints and then model choice from the library.
issues.next_step: Finish the block fingerprints (in progress), then model choice.

issues.title: Everything is verified on one computer, one pedal firmware, with a private helper
issues.problem: Pedal control is verified on macOS and firmware 3.80 only, and the small helper program that talks to the pedal is intentionally not published.
issues.impact: Other users on Windows or Linux may not be able to use pedal mode, and others cannot reproduce the pedal measurements.
issues.cause: Only one machine is available, and the helper's source is withheld on the owner's decision.
issues.resolution: Publish a wrapper or rewrite the helper to the documented protocol; test on other systems when machines exist.

issues.impact: It decides whether models trained on Native renders may be published; it blocks nothing until the learning stage.
issues.cause: Recording the finding was left to the owner.
issues.resolution: Write the relevant clauses' conclusions into the licence notes.
issues.next_step: Covered by the owner action about the licence agreements.

issues.title: No blind listening has happened (the tool is now built)
issues.problem: The only listening so far was informal and unblinded. The blind A/B tool is built but has not been used in a session.
issues.impact: Whether matches sound better than a ready-made preset is still unknown; Gate 4 cannot start.
issues.cause: Sessions need matched presets from the whole pipeline, which does not exist yet.
issues.resolution: Run sessions once the pipeline produces candidates; an optional short listen can accompany the Gate 2 review.

Synthetic known-answer data on Native; not real songs; the ear has not judged it.

recent_changes.text: Gate 2 attempt 3 met all 7 checks on the 96 sealed items: category 0.885, model 0.771, settings error 0.101, ranking the true preset first 0.979 under the owner's extended rule, better than the random walk on model and settings. The gate is not passed until the owner signs. Delay (5 of 12 exact models) is now the weakest effect.

Gate 2 attempt 2 did not pass: 6 of 7 checks on the 96 sealed items. Category 0.865 (was 0.802), model 0.760 (was 0.646), settings error 0.091, better than the random walk on both model and settings, consistency split passes. Ranking the true preset first fails at 0.9375 against 0.95 (was 0.990): six misses on amp, drive and one cabinet, which the middle baseline shares. Modulation and drive are weakest; cabinet and equaliser are perfect. The rule is unchanged and v2 is now seen.

The human approved the next improvement round for Gate 2 attempt 3: a gain-stage score term, drive and modulation specialists, and a fresh sealed synthetic-v3 (generated and sealed since). Synthetic-v2 is now spent: diagnosis only, never used to admit a change.

Specialists were adopted for four families: cabinet and equaliser (model 24 of 24 on development items against 18 of 24 for the general method), time-based effects (held-out model 14 to 19), amp (param error 0.224 to 0.120), and a dispatcher plus adapters that route each family to its specialist. Gate 2 attempt 2 ran on all of them; category and model rose accordingly.

Parallel jobs now survive restarts (an item-level queue, workers grow and shrink with the host scaler), the Native host cap was raised from 6 to 8 on the human's instruction, and a false silence alarm on a very quiet true preset (item i062) was fixed; i062 stays in the set as a normal item.

Gate 2 attempt 1 did not pass. On all 96 items: model 0.646, settings error 0.132, ranking 0.990 and settings better than the random walk pass; category 0.802 (bar 0.85) and model non-inferiority to the random walk (low end -0.083, needs -0.05) fail. The 80 untuned items agree. Strong families: drive, cabinet, compressor, delay; weak: modulation, reverb, amp. The next attempt uses a fresh set and per-family specialists.

The human directed a specialist per effect family, with single blocks first and chains built from analysis, no full-library test, trained weights may be published, and the cabinet-response library may be used for training. The 19 non-impulse-response recordings were removed from the library folder to the Trash. The pass rule was frozen before the run, and the baseline "random search" is now called the random walk.

Native is verified for Gate 2: three engine bugs were fixed (baked controls, hosts in the other rounding mode, an amp state latch), repeatability is 216 of 216, nothing is unexplained, and an in-run sentinel now guards long jobs. Recorded misses (116 of 120 setting-truth pairs, 63 of 73 baked renders) are one-step rounding and input/output blocks.

The pedal verification found real sampling defects: unstable USB audio for about 0.7 s after start, amp state carried between renders, four models refused, and a slow in-place glide on some delay and reverb settings. A longer pre-roll fixed the first; a one-sample slip remains in about 1 render in 90. No pedal result counts until it is handled.

Search got measured seeding (the target's own delay time, reverb decay and modulation rate set the starting point) and then a hybrid method with broad draws, narrowing and refinement, chosen by a rule fixed before the last run. On the 16 development items model accuracy went from 6 to 13 of 16 over the day (development only, not gate evidence).
Baselines were recorded: the middle-of-every-knob guess and the random walk. The random walk scores high because it has 300 tries over a 47-model pool judged by the trusted score.

The curated preset corpus (2,068 presets after cleaning) gave strong order rules, super-groups and heavy concentration of model use; descriptive metadata adds little. Only category-level statistics are committed.

The cabinet impulse-response library analysis shows that estimating a cabinet by deconvolution is promising: the pedal's cabinet is the top match in 22 of 24 real-clip tests when the amp is right. It is useless with the wrong amp. No library data leaves the machine.

The block-presence detector, scored once on its test split, passed only for the cabinet and for whether a gain stage is present. It is used as a soft hint only; time-based blocks are confirmed by rendering with and without them.

A chain builder (tested with fake engines) and a blind A/B listening tool were built, and a local Gate 2 explainer for a non-technical reader was added (kept off the public repository). None of these changes a gate on its own.

The two engine items that were held back (out-of-range values and a real-guitar smoke test) are done: the real-guitar smoke test passes on Native. On-demand capture defaults off after it opened an editor window per preset.
Model choice tied the old pool pass at 7 of 16 development models under the old provisional score. This was superseded on 2026-10-17: the baselines are now recorded and the hybrid search replaced it.

The Native verification suite first showed one of 216 repeat renders at -97.4 dB against the -100 dB line. The cause was a state carried between models (an amp latch), plus baked controls and a rounding mode. After three engine fixes repeatability is 216 of 216 (worst -161.5 dB), with an in-run sentinel in place.

Native block fingerprints were measured for 602 of 605 library models (24 of about 3,600 settings were silent, all expected), and rendering many candidates at once is 1.46 times faster than one at a time with identical results. Model choice per slot is built.

The pedal's two-variant pass equals serial renders on firmware 3.80 and is about 1.7 times faster per variant (1.70 s against about 2.9 s). This closes the audio check that was open last report. Pedal restores are now judged by decoded equality, since raw bytes can differ by 3 after the pedal re-encodes.

A chain-pattern prior was built from 129 presets: drive comes before amp in 55 of 55 presets with both, amp before cab 90 of 90, delay before reverb in 96 percent. It is aggregate statistics only; no preset content is committed. It is not yet used by a chain builder.

New direction from the human: single blocks first, with chains built from analysis of real presets (which kinds of block are present, ordered by common patterns). The curated preset and cabinet-IR libraries stay local and are never committed; the song-metadata lookup (artist and title only) is approved as opt-in.

The human chose the Gate 2 scoring rules (tune the measure for the known-recording case; count identical-sounding look-alikes as ties) and waived the 'right chain structure' target for Gate 2, which now covers single blocks only. Chain structure moves to Gate 4. Scoring rules 2 and 3 are coded.

The tone comparison was admitted for single blocks when the clean recording is known. Tuned on a train split and scored once on a held-out split of 96 items, it ranked the true preset first 0.990 of the time against a bar of 0.90 (older measure 0.781), counting identical-sounding look-alikes as ties. The tuning score matched the test score, so it was not overfit. This replaces the failed first check as the main evidence for that case only.

The first trust check on real Helix sound failed: no tone-comparison measure picks the true preset reliably. On new notes the best managed about 7 times in 40 against a bar of 36; the measures react more to the notes played than to the tone. With the same notes and a lined-up recording one measure reached 0.725 (0.875 if look-alikes that sound identical are ignored). This replaces the earlier stand-in result as the main evidence and is now the biggest problem.

The software engine now holds 605 of the pedal's 607 effect models as single-block templates (the other 2 are refused by Native). Every template was replayed in a fresh host. This opens model choice from a library, but the blocks are not yet measured.

Delay times in the software engine now move in 10 ms steps instead of 63 ms, because Native honours a narrower control range. Block Level was also given a finer range (0.25 dB steps with 0 dB on the grid).

The measurements settled where the software engine can stand in for the pedal: amps, cabinets, dynamics, equalisers, most drives, delays, four reverb types, Hall above 500 Hz and the modulation effects. The pedal still checks Ganymede-type reverbs, Hall on bass-heavy material, Bitcrusher-type drives and Early Reflections. A suggested delay-time correction of under 1 in 100 was rejected: the apparent error was Native's control step, not an engine difference.

Two chains in one pedal pass give the same sound as one chain per pass on firmware 3.80, and code to render two chains per pass was written. Its audio comparison has not run because the Mac's audio failed during the session. Update: the audio comparison was later run and passed (see the 2026-10-16 entry on the pedal's two-variant pass).
The separation stress curve is recorded on a synthetic mix: guitar-only quality 21.2 dB falls to 7.3 dB with a second guitar. This ticks one Gate 2 item but says nothing yet about real songs.

The known-answer harness (96 one-block presets) was built and a 3-item run made. The run is provisional and not gate evidence; its first version scored the true preset against itself and was voided and re-run.

The search keeps scoring the full clip: shorter clips did worse in the clip-length study. Two-chain passes on Native are out of scope (decided by the owner), and time-variant blocks are opt-in for search.

Pedal engine work: a shared pedal lock with a device check, layout-changing loads written whole with read-back, and the Simple Delay Scale report explained (not a fault). A pedal session had control steps pass but audio fail (Mac audio down); the pedal was restored. These are not yet committed.

The pedal's blocks no longer stay locked after a control session. The helper now ends each session the way the pedal's own editing program does; a person confirmed the blocks were editable afterwards on firmware 3.80, where the lock had still occurred before the fix.

The pedal now runs firmware 3.80. Its engine smoke test passes there, and 9 of 9 whole-preset writes (including amps with impulse-response cabinets and one block from each effect category) landed and the pedal was restored byte for byte. Pedal-versus-Native agreement has not yet been re-measured on 3.80.
Gate 1 was signed off: both engines are driven by code and a generated preset loads on the pedal.
Helix Native now loads new sounds without a person at the keyboard and renders about seven times faster, and it stopped running out of memory.
The pedal write is now checked parameter by parameter. This traced and fixed a bug that made a delay run far too wet when the owner played a preset live on the pedal.
A first real song section was matched end to end and loaded on the pedal. The result was informal progress, not a validation.
Rendering a chain one block at a time matched rendering it whole on a test chain, which opens the way to measuring blocks individually.
A new problem was found: one cabinet setting sounds different on the pedal and in Native. Presets for the pedal keep it at 0 for now.
The first real-song run showed the tone score is not reliable: its top two candidates were almost tied and the listener preferred one clearly.
A silent bug that could reuse an outdated Native setup (and made one measurement look much worse than it was) was found and fixed; the false result was voided.

Two extra tone-comparison measures were added (a sharper loudness-shape measure and a learned audio embedding). Neither came close to the target on stand-in signals, so they did not move Gate 2 forward.
The block measuring kit was finished offline. It has not touched Helix yet, so it does not advance readiness until it is run.
The owner approved the per-block approach (measure and search block by block). It adds work before Gate 2 but shrinks the search space.

Checking candidates on the pedal got much faster: a search trial went from 10.9 s to 3.8 s and the per-test session overhead from 3.81 s to 0.77 s. A verification finalist improved less, from 29.2 s to 24.7 s. The search now uses these options by default (task T062), but how much that speeds a real search has not yet been timed on the pedal. These timings are on one pedal with one chain type; they say nothing about match quality.

Helix Native's speed work (T055) is finished. Capturing a new chain fell from about 31 s to 1.2 s in one session and 0.39 s with three sessions (216 blocks in 84.6 s). A pool of 6 parallel hosts runs 9.9 two-second tests per second (4.6 on ten-second clips); 10 hosts did a little better but with memory pressure and swapping, so the cap is 6. Bypass by MIDI control still matches separate captures (-328.7 dB), and a fault where about 1 host in 10 rendered differently is now caught by a start-up check. Measured on one Mac; nothing here has been judged by ear.

Follow-up Native work (T064): the two template sets used for matching (B and B0) were re-captured with Hum and Ripple at 0, so the matcher has all 7 test candidates under both engine policies. A scan of 607 pedal block models found only 2 that Native 3.82 refuses to load, so nearly the whole catalog can be captured for Native; the library itself is still not captured.

The pedal's two-path layout difference is fixed (T063). Our two-path version of a stored preset used to cancel against the one saved by the pedal's editor at only -9.3 dB; it now cancels at -85.7 dB, the same as the editor's preset repeated against itself. Single-path loads are unchanged. Measured on firmware 3.80, one preset, one pedal.

The rule that two-path renders may only be compared with two-path renders is lifted, because after the layout fix a two-path pass matches single-chain renders (Path A -72.9 dB against a repeat floor of -68.7; Path B -52.6 against -42.7). Two chains per pass can be used for checks; the 2.0x gain was measured on firmware 3.50 and is not re-measured on 3.80.

Decided by the owner: the amp's Hum and Ripple settings are frozen at 0 on both engines. They added a free-running noise that made two renders of the same preset differ at about -30 dB (against -72 to -91 dB at 0), which hid real differences and blocked the shorter pedal waits. This closes the open question and removes it from the owner's action list.

Decided by the owner: Helix Native runs at most 6 hosts at once (measured on 32 GB of memory: green memory pressure at 6, yellow with swapping at 8 and 10). All Native pool figures in this report are for 6 hosts.

Decided by the owner: Native results from before 2026-10-16 are kept as history and not re-run wholesale. About 1 host in 10 had rendered differently and delay trims could differ by up to 30 samples. The results we rely on are re-measured in the parity spot checks and the Gate 2 benchmark.

The continuous-integration build (the automatic test run on GitHub) was fixed in commit 07b66ed: one test that needs a local-only file is skipped when the file is absent. It changes no product capability.

components.name: Sound engines: Helix Native and the HX Stomp pedal
components.purpose: Turn a candidate preset and a clean guitar clip into sound, so candidates can be compared. Native is fast and offline; the pedal is the real thing.
components.works: Both engines are driven from code on macOS. Native is verified for Gate 2: exact settings apart from explained misses, 216 of 216 repeat renders, a sentinel against drift. The pedal two-variant pass, whole-preset writes and decoded-equality restores work.
components.missing: Windows and Linux, stereo blocks, the cabinet Early Reflections setting, some reverb and drive types. Pedal verification is incomplete: four refused models, a slow glide on some settings, and a one-sample slip in about 1 render in 90.
components.problem: No pedal measurement counts until the residual slip is handled.
components.next: Detect or re-take slipped pedal renders, then fix the refusals and the glide, then re-register and re-run the pedal rules.
components.confidence: Native: hardware-measured on one Mac, 9,770 renders in the verification. Pedal: hardware, firmware 3.80, with recorded failures; ear not involved.

components.name: Preset files and the block catalog
components.purpose: Read, write and validate the preset files the pedal and Native load.
components.works: Reference files round-trip exactly, models are read from the owner's own install, generated files load, and a chain-pattern prior built from 2,068 curated presets (category-level statistics only) shows strong order rules.
components.missing: Building up to three snapshots from a match, and forcing snapshot values to equal block values inside the writer.
components.problem: A stale snapshot value can silently change the sound; the rule 'block values win' is applied in scripts but not yet in the writer.
components.next: Move the snapshot synchronisation into the preset writer.
components.confidence: Round trip tested on two reference files; one generated preset loaded on the pedal.

components.name: Preparing the song: guitar isolation and a clean reference guitar
components.purpose: Extract the guitar from the recording and supply a clean guitar recording to compare against.
components.works: Separation runs in seconds, sections are found and a library of clean guitar clips is indexed. A stress curve on a synthetic mix is recorded.
components.missing: Any quality score on real songs and any measurement of the clean-guitar choice's benefit.
components.problem: Separation quality on real songs is unknown.
components.next: Stress-test on a few real songs once the owner chooses them.
components.confidence: Synthetic mix only; one real song without a quality score.

components.name: Judging tone similarity: comparison measures and block measuring
components.purpose: Say how close two guitar sounds are, and describe how each block behaves.
components.works: Five comparison measures run. One (the multi-resolution spectral measure, version 2) is admitted for single blocks with a known clean recording (0.990). A block-presence detector exists (cabinet and gain stage pass; the rest miss). A cabinet-response estimator is promising. Block fingerprints exist for 602 models.
components.missing: A measure for the no-recording song case; reliable detection of delay, reverb and modulation blocks.
components.problem: The comparison is admitted only for the known-recording case. The score ranks the true preset first on 90 of 96 sealed items (bar 0.95): gain-stage neighbours score alike.
components.next: Add a gain-stage score term that passes loss-trust on gain neighbours (running).
components.confidence: Real Helix renders from Native; held-out splits scored once; synthetic known-answer data, not real songs or ears.

components.name: Searching for the preset and the song-to-preset pipeline
components.purpose: Try candidate presets, score them against the target and return the best preset.
components.works: A hybrid method with family specialists (cabinet and equaliser, time-based, modulation, amp, gain) runs on Native. On 96 sealed items it named the category 88.5 percent and the model 77.1 percent of the time with settings error 0.101 (attempt 3). A chain builder exists, tested with fake engines only.
components.missing: Delay (model 5 of 12) and drive (7 of 12) are weak. Chain builder on a real engine, snapshots for several sections, a one-command tool.
components.problem: Weak on delay and drive; delay is the biggest gap now.
components.next: Diagnose and strengthen the delay specialist on development data.
components.confidence: Synthetic known-answer data (96 sealed items) on Native; one informal listen on one real song.

components.name: Testing, benchmarks and listening
components.purpose: Provide the measurements and listening tests that decide whether the product works.
components.works: The evidence ledger, smoke tests, engine agreement measurements, the 96-item known-answer set with its runner and frozen pass rule, three full attempt results (the third meets all checks), and a blind A/B session tool.
components.missing: The human's Gate 2 sign-off, fresh sets for later work, a rated blind session.
components.problem: Three sealed sets are now spent; Gate 2 is awaiting sign-off.
components.next: Prepare listening on the delay misses; build development sets for delay work.
components.confidence: Hardware measurements of engine agreement; full known-answer runs on Native; listening informal only.

components.name: Learning from data
components.purpose: Learn good starting points so the search needs fewer renders.
components.missing: Everything; it depends on a trusted comparison and on the licence findings.

components.name: Foundations: installation, licensing and the working process
components.purpose: Make the project installable, legally clean and organised.
components.works: Installs on this Mac, licence checks pass, and the board, evidence ledger and gates are in use.
components.missing: Windows and Linux checks, recorded licence-agreement findings, and tidier board lines.
components.problem: Licence-agreement findings are unrecorded; some board lines are stale.
components.next: Update the board; owner records the licence findings.

glossary.definition: Direct Input: a clean, unprocessed guitar recording, before any amp or effects.
Digital Signal Processing: the audio calculations inside amps and effects.
The software licence agreement shown when installing a product.
An optimisation algorithm used to search for suitable settings.
The Line 6 guitar-effects pedal this project targets.
Line 6's software version of the Helix sounds; it runs as a plugin and renders audio offline.
Line 6's editing program for the pedal; it also imports preset files.
A saved sound: a chain of amp, cabinet and effect blocks with their settings (an .hlx file).
One of up to three stored variations of a preset that the pedal can switch between.
The software running inside the pedal.
The score the optimiser tries to lower: how different two sounds are. Lower is a closer match.
The loss: the combined measures of how similar two guitar sounds are.
Test audio made by ordinary software effects instead of Helix. Useful for early checks; not proof the method works on Helix.
A test set made by rendering presets we already know through Helix, so we can check whether the tool recovers them.
Test items not used when tuning, so the result is not flattered by tuning.
A test of whether a measure puts the true preset first among many candidates.
What is left when one recording is subtracted from another that should match. Reported in decibels below the signal; the more negative, the closer.
Decibel, a logarithmic loudness or level-difference scale.
A cabinet setting that adds the first short echoes of the room.
Splitting a full mix into instruments so the guitar can be analysed alone.
One element in a preset's chain: an amp, cabinet, drive pedal, delay and so on.
The project's append-only record of measured runs; a claim without a row did not happen.
A milestone with a written checklist and a human sign-off.
A listening test where the listener does not know which option is which.
Reading the pedal's settings back after writing them to confirm they match.
A control message that moves one knob or switch from software.
Short for firmware, the pedal's built-in software. The pedal was on version 3.50 until 2026-10-15 and is now on 3.80.
Play a test signal through a preset and record the audio that comes out.
The one-off step that teaches Helix Native a new chain: the preset file is loaded into its editor and the resulting state is recorded.
Agreement between the two engines: the same preset is rendered on both and the recordings are compared.
Several copies of Helix Native running at once, each rendering a different candidate, to finish a batch sooner.
Extra audio played before the part that is recorded, so delays and reverbs start from the same state every time.
The two signal paths of the HX Stomp. Using both at once renders two chains in one pass.
Two amp settings that add a mains-hum style noise. The noise runs freely, so it differs between renders of the same preset.
The last message a control program sends to the pedal when it is done. Without it the pedal stays in editing mode and its blocks cannot be edited by hand.
One candidate setting tried by the search: it is rendered and then scored against the target.
A reference preset file the owner exported from HX Edit or Native, used to check that our own files follow the same layout.
Real elapsed time on a clock, as opposed to computing time.
How often the true preset is ranked first among the candidates (the look-alikes). Higher is better; guessing among 20 gives 0.05.
A stored set of single-block Native setups, one per pedal effect model, used to build and render candidate presets quickly.
The Mac's audio system. When it fails, no sound can be sent to or recorded from the pedal.
A candidate preset that differs slightly from the true one (a nearby setting or a neighbouring model); used to test whether a measure can tell near matches apart.
An effect that changes its sound on its own over time (for example a free-running chorus), so two renders never cancel exactly.

A baseline search that tries 300 random settings and keeps the best, judged by the same trusted score. It scores high here because the tool has only 300 tries over a pool of 47 effect models and the score is a good judge, so even random guessing often lands on the right model. Earlier notes called it random search.
A baseline that sets every knob to the middle of its range and picks nothing cleverly. It shows what a do-nothing guess scores.
A separate method for one family of effects (gain, linear, dynamics, time-based, modulation) with its own measurements and search, instead of one general method for everything.
A group of effects that behave alike: gain (drive, fuzz, amp), linear (cabinet, equaliser), dynamics (compressor, gate), time-based (delay, reverb), modulation (chorus, flanger, phaser, tremolo).
A range for a measured difference, built by re-sampling the 96 items many times. If the whole range sits on the good side of a line, the difference is reliable at the stated confidence.
A check run inside a long job that renders a fixed test now and then and stops the job if the result has drifted, so a corrupted render cannot be scored as real.
The planned stage that decides which kinds of block a tone needs, orders them by common patterns learned from real presets, and then fills each slot using the single-block methods.
A fresh known-answer set, made with the same generator and the same frozen rules but a new random seed, because the first set has now been seen.
A short recording of a speaker cabinet and microphone that can reproduce that cabinet's sound by convolution. A cabinet block in the pedal uses one.
Helix Native starts each session in one of two slightly different rounding modes. The difference is tiny (rounding level) but can break exact cancellation tests.
A one-sample shift or short burst in the audio coming back from the pedal over its USB connection, which makes a render differ slightly from an identical earlier one.

engines._about: Wording for the 'Engines: what each can do and how fast' section. The capability verdicts are curated judgements from the ledger, DECISIONS, notes and board (cite them inline; they become links). Numbers written as {t:key:engine} are filled from the ledger every run, so they cannot go stale. 'fw350': true appends 'verified on fw 3.50, recheck on 3.80 pending' until a ledger row shows the claim re-checked on firmware 3.80; then the flag is cleared (done for parameter changes and two-path rendering on 2026-10-16). All timings and the 100-test estimates are computed by scripts/engine_timing.py; nothing about time is written by hand here.
engines.units: Times are in seconds (s), minutes (min) and hours (h). A render is one pass of a test signal through a preset, recorded as audio. A score is one comparison of a rendered candidate against the target tone (lower is better). A capture is the one-off step that teaches Helix Native a new chain, by loading the preset file into its editor and recording its state. A parity check renders one preset on both engines and compares the two recordings. Estimates are 100 times the newest measured time; every estimate says which measurement it uses and its date. Native pool figures use 6 hosts (the owner approved that cap on 2026-10-16) and count a render plus its score as one test; pedal figures from firmware 3.80 are marked as such.

render_2s.label: One render of a 2 s test clip
render_2s.means: Play a 2 second test signal through a preset and record the result.

search_test.label: One search test, 2 s clip
search_test.means: One candidate in a search. Native: a render plus its score through the 6-host pool. Pedal: one search trial with the T061 speed options (3 s clip), render side only.

search_test_10s.label: One search test, 10 s clip
search_test_10s.means: The same with a 10 s excerpt. Pedal: the trial before the T061 speed options, for comparison.

session.label: Pedal session overhead
session.means: Opening the pedal engine, restoring the original preset and checking it byte for byte. Once per batch since T061.

verify.label: Verify one finalist on the pedal
verify.means: Write a finalist whole to the pedal and render it twice with 10 s clips.

render_10s.label: One render of a 10 s clip
render_10s.means: The same, with a 10 second excerpt (the size a song-section search uses).

score.label: One comparison (score) of a candidate against a target
score.means: Measure how far a rendered candidate is from the target tone. From the trust check's scoring-cost rows: the three signal-processing terms added, render excluded.

parity.label: One parity comparison (per preset)
parity.means: Render one preset on both engines, then analyse how closely the two recordings agree.

smoke.label: One engine smoke test
smoke.means: The quick end-to-end check that an engine loads a preset and returns sound.

search_run.label: A search run, per trial
search_run.means: Native: the run's wall clock divided by its renders, engine start-up included. Pedal: seconds per trial of the default search run (3 s clip).

load.label: One preset load or model change
load.means: Stomp: one whole-document write of a generated preset. Native: load a stored template.

capture.label: First-time capture of a new chain
capture.means: Native only: teach the engine a chain it has not seen. Once per chain.

probe_pass.label: One probe pass through an engine
probe_pass.means: Play the block-probe test signals through one block and record them.

probe_analysis.label: One probe analysis (offline)
probe_analysis.means: Check the probe analysis code against known software blocks; no engine involved.

trial.label: One search trial (render + score)
trial.means: One candidate setting: render it, then score it. Scoring time is taken from the score row above.

combined_testing.label: Combined: testing
combined_testing.means: Engine smoke test per engine, and one parity comparison per preset on both.

combined_comparison.label: Combined: comparison
combined_comparison.means: Scoring a candidate against a target.

combined_modelling.label: Combined: modelling
combined_modelling.means: One search trial plus a capture (Native) or a preset write (Stomp).

capabilities.capability: Load a generated preset file (.hlx) directly

stomp.verdict: Yes. The file is compiled and written whole into the pedal's working memory, then read back parameter by parameter before anything is rendered; about 40 whole writes, all read back as written (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 Stomp T056 outcomes). 4 of 4 generated files were written and rendered (ledger 2026-10-14T23:47:43+00:00). Re-checked on firmware 3.80: 9 of 9 whole writes landed and the pedal was restored byte for byte (ledger 2026-10-15T23:40:20+00:00). Takes {t:load:stomp}.

native.verdict: Yes, with no person, on macOS: a script drops the file into Native's editor and records the state as a template, then renders from the template (ledger 2026-10-14T23:58:32+00:00). A stored template loads in {t:load:native}; a chain never seen before needs a capture first (see below).

capabilities.capability: Export or save a preset file

stomp.verdict: Our own writer produces the .hlx; a human imports it in HX Edit (accepted, ledger 2026-10-14T17:38:00+00:00). The engine never saves to the pedal's flash memory, by policy: it edits the working copy only and puts the original preset back (DECISIONS 2026-10-14 stomp-engine, T003 hardware batch and T004).

native.verdict: Not done and not needed for matching: the generated .hlx is the source, and Native's captured state is kept as a local template, not exported as a file.

stomp.verdict: Yes, at full resolution. Parameters are set in place and checked by read-back to within one hundred-thousandth of the parameter's range (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 stomp-engine, T051 whole-write readback). Re-checked on firmware 3.80: 20 in-place loads of six random amp parameters each ended with a clean full read-back (ledger 2026-10-15T23:57:03+00:00).

native.verdict: Only parameters given a MIDI control number at capture, in 128 steps across each range; everything else stays as captured. Inside that grid it equals a freshly captured file almost exactly (ledger 2026-10-15T20:46:58+00:00). On the 8-block test chain 54 of 63 mapped parameters moved the sound (ledger 2026-10-15T21:31:30+00:00).

capabilities.capability: Change models (swap an amp, cab or effect)

stomp.verdict: Yes. Any model or layout change is one whole write with read-back, never the pedal's own model command (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 Stomp T056 outcomes). {t:load:stomp} per write. On firmware 3.80, one block from each of the six effect categories and two amps with impulse-response cabinets were built and read back (ledger 2026-10-15T23:40:20+00:00).

native.verdict: Yes, from the block library: a model is loaded by its id from a stored template, with no new capture. Chains of several blocks still need a capture ({t:capture:native}, once per chain). Mono only (ledger 2026-10-16T15:25:12+00:00).

capabilities.capability: Switch blocks on and off by script

stomp.verdict: Yes. Bypass is toggled in place with a MIDI control (the delay's bypass moved with CC 110, ledger 2026-10-15T21:14:14+00:00), and is part of every whole write.

native.verdict: Yes. Each block's bypass is a MIDI control number in the captured template; one capture reproduces every bypass pattern almost exactly (-328.7 dB against files captured one by one, ledger 2026-10-15T21:31:30+00:00). Only chains captured since 2026-10-15 have it; older templates keep fixed bypass states (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 native-engine, Native phase 2 block bypass).

stomp.verdict: Path A and Path B give twice the renders per pass (measured on firmware 3.50, ledger 2026-10-15T21:14:14+00:00; not re-measured on 3.80). The earlier gap of -18 to -22 dB between two-path and single-path renders was a layout bug, fixed by writing the layout the way the pedal's own editor stores it: on firmware 3.80 our two-path load now nulls against the editor-saved preset at -85.7 dB, equal to that preset's own repeat floor, against -9.3 dB before (ledger 2026-10-16T01:06:38+00:00). A two-path pass also matches each chain rendered alone: Path A -72.9 dB (repeat floor -68.7), Path B -52.6 dB (floor -42.7). The rule that two-path renders are compared only with two-path renders was lifted on 2026-10-16 (DECISIONS 2026-10-16 stomp-engine, T063 two-path layout). Not tested: crossover and A/B split types; a pass with its own Path B input is refused by the compiler. Two-chain passes equal single-chain passes on firmware 3.80 for the tested chains (ledger 2026-10-16T15:44:03+00:00). The code that renders two variants per pass was then compared on the pedal's audio against serial renders: path A/B nulls of -78.5/-60.4 and -85.1/-78.6 dB, each below the serial repeat floor, about 1.7 s per variant (ledger 2026-10-16T20:28:58+00:00).

native.verdict: Out of scope: two-path passes on Native will not be built (owner's decision, 2026-10-16); Native renders in parallel on 6 hosts instead. Block-serial chaining equals one instance at -67 to -79 dB above 20 Hz on the tested chains (ledger 2026-10-15T19:21:10+00:00).

capabilities.capability: Use the whole block and model catalog

stomp.verdict: In principle any compatible model can be written with no capture, because the pedal runs it itself. Tried so far: the amps, cabs, drives and delays in the test presets on firmware 3.50, and one block from each effect category and two amps with impulse-response cabinets on firmware 3.80 (ledger 2026-10-15T23:40:20+00:00). Whether the 90 models gated by firmware now work on 3.80 has not been rechecked (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 Stomp firmware upgrade, human).

native.verdict: Through the per-block library, now captured: 605 of the pedal's 607 models (the other 2, a transient shaper and a poly bass whammy, are refused by Native 3.82), each replayed in a fresh host (ledger 2026-10-16T15:25:12+00:00). Time-like and rate settings were re-captured with narrower control ranges (ledger 2026-10-16T16:04:28+00:00, 2026-10-16T17:54:03+00:00). Not captured by design: routing models and the second cabinet of a dual-cab block.

stomp.verdict: {t:render_2s:stomp} for a 2 s clip (the pedal plays the audio in real time); a 10 s clip is {t:render_10s:stomp}. Two-chain passes double throughput (see above). Measured on firmware 3.80: a 3 s clip takes 3.67 s (ledger 2026-10-15T23:48:50+00:00). A search trial with the T061 speed options takes {t:search_test:stomp} (render side only). See the speed-up row below for the search and verification gains.

native.verdict: {t:render_2s:native} for a 2 s clip and {t:render_10s:native} for a 10 s clip including 3 s of pre-roll. A pool of 6 parallel hosts (the approved cap) finishes a search test of a 2 s clip, render and score together, in {t:search_test:native}, and one of a 10 s clip in {t:search_test_10s:native} (timing tables below).

stomp.verdict: Snapshot values are written into the document and must equal the block values (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 snapshot values, lead on stomp-engine T051). Switching snapshots by MIDI (CC 69) recalls the stored values (ledger 2026-10-15T21:14:14+00:00). Switching during a render is not tested.

native.verdict: Native renders the block values and ignores snapshot values when a file is loaded (ledger 2026-10-15T19:42:45+00:00). Snapshots are not switched in Native.

both.verdict: Measured on firmware 3.80 (ledger 2026-10-16T02:31:10+00:00, 2026-10-16T15:36:36+00:00, 2026-10-16T16:18:35+00:00): amps cancel at -37.5 to -47.5 dB and cabinets at -35.4 to -37.4 dB (pass line -30 dB); dynamics and equalisers pass. For delays, reverbs and modulation the comparison is by echo timing, decay and modulation rate rather than cancellation. Accepted result: Native stands in for amps, cabinets, dynamics, equalisers, drives except Bitcrusher-type, delays, four reverb types, Hall above 500 Hz, and the modulation effects; the pedal still checks Ganymede-type reverbs, Hall on bass-heavy material, Bitcrusher-type drives and cabinet Early Reflections. A suggested delay-time scaling of under 1 in 100 was rejected (it was Native's control step).

stomp.verdict: The session-release lock is fixed (T059). Before the fix any control session left the pedal's block editing locked until USB was unplugged, even after the firmware 3.80 upgrade (ledger 2026-10-15T22:36:17+00:00). The helper now sends HX Edit's session close, and a person confirmed the blocks were editable afterwards (ledger 2026-10-15T23:03:12+00:00); the close was answered on every channel in a later smoke run (ledger 2026-10-15T23:20:15+00:00). One earlier control wedge that needed a power cycle is still unexplained (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 HX Stomp priorities, human). Pedal verification on 2026-10-17 (ledger 2026-10-17T17:37:28+00:00): setting truth 20 of 40, repeatability 12 of 17; the audio stream is unstable for about 0.7 s after start, amps carry state between renders, four models are refused, and a one-sample slip remains in about 1 render in 90. Pre-roll is now 1.0 s (2.0 s with an amp). No pedal result counts until that slip is handled.

native.verdict: Memory growth and crashes are fixed: the host stays at about 3.0 GB and repeats are identical to -313 dB (ledger 2026-10-15T18:54:10+00:00; DECISIONS 2026-10-15 native-engine, host memory). About 1 host process in 10 rendered every chain differently until a start-up check (the host canary) began replacing such hosts (ledger 2026-10-16T00:25:27+00:00); Native results from before 2026-10-16 are kept as history. Captures need a logged-in screen session. Verification on 2026-10-17 (ledger 2026-10-17T17:35:18+00:00): repeat renders 216 of 216 at worst -161.5 dB after three engine fixes (baked controls no longer sent, hosts in the other numeric mode re-prepared, an amp state latch at open); setting truth 116 of 120 pairs (ledger 2026-10-17T17:38:13+00:00); a sentinel in the engine catches a forced drift (ledger 2026-10-17T17:29:36+00:00). Native results from before these fixes used the earlier engine.

stomp.verdict: Measured on firmware 3.80 (T061, docs/notes/stomp-speed.md): a search trial went from 10.861 s to 3.765 s (ledger 2026-10-16T00:17:11+00:00, 10 trials, 3 s clips, readback every 10 loads, measured tail waits). Per-test session overhead fell from 3.812 s to 0.772 s (ledger 2026-10-15T23:47:32+00:00). A verification finalist (whole write plus two 10 s renders) improved only from 29.23 s to 24.65 s (ledger 2026-10-16T00:10:35+00:00). The shorter tail waits are only equal to the long waits with Hum and Ripple at 0 (ledger 2026-10-15T23:55:24+00:00). The search now uses these options by default (task T062), but it has not been timed on the pedal.

native.verdict: Capture fell from about 31 s to 1.2 s per chain in one session, and 216 chains took 84.6 s (ledger 2026-10-15T23:57:11+00:00). A pool of 6 hosts ran 9.9 tests per second on 2 s clips and 4.6 on 10 s clips (ledger 2026-10-16T00:38:03+00:00); 10 hosts ran 13.1 and 6.4 but with memory pressure and swapping, so the owner capped the pool at 6 on 2026-10-16. Newest batch capture: 391 single-block chains at 0.22 s each in 3 sessions with the parameter checks off (ledger 2026-10-16T00:58:52+00:00). About 1 host in 10 rendered differently until a start-up check replaced it (ledger 2026-10-16T00:25:27+00:00). The timing tables below read these newer rows.

stomp.verdict: Tested on macOS only. Linux is expected to work and Windows is unconfirmed; both are set aside for now (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 HX Stomp priorities, human). The pedal is now on firmware 3.80: its smoke test and whole writes pass there (ledger 2026-10-15T23:20:15+00:00), but parity with Native and the firmware-gated models are not yet re-measured (spot checks T060 are next).

native.verdict: Tested on macOS with Native 3.82 as a VST3 plug-in in a helper process. Other platforms untested. Real MIDI control into the AU build did not change parameters (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 native-engine, Native phase 2 block bypass).
